correctness.rationale: Exact deterministic affine weight normalization, a correctly normalized independent categorical surrogate and equality of all leaf-set transition probabilities prove the finite path law. The one-hot negative association closure argument proves the full arbitrary-horizon statement and an exponential-moment argument proves concentration. Explicit conditioning gives nonpositive covariances for all positive kernels through four vertices and a rational five-vertex covariance with unique positive threshold. The packaged checker passed 1,272 exact finite and symbolic assertions; infinite-size conclusions rely on the analytic proof.

originality.rationale: The novel claim is the exact representation of the full individual leaf-survival process for degree-reinforced affine attachment and the sharp first nonlinear failure. The underlying general occupancy negative-association theorem is explicitly credited, not repackaged as new. Inspected full texts establish aggregate leaf, degree/leafdegree, or independent-parent pairwise results, and do not imply the attachment-process representation or the five-vertex threshold without additional mathematics.

value.rationale: This is a complete exact labeled leaf-survival law for every finite size and distinct vertex-specific observation horizon, yielding joint probabilities, negative association and useful nonasymptotic subgroup concentration. The earliest possible positive leaf covariance under nonlinear reinforcement is pinned to five vertices, and the threshold is exact for an explicitly motivated minimal positive kernel. The result explains where a structural negative-dependence property changes rather than calculating an arbitrary rare invariant.
